system:
You review benchmark items against the knowledge atom each one tests. The items test whether a model knows the atom (recall and recognition), and the test taker sees only the question and options.

Judge each item on the checks listed on its CHECKS line. Rules:
- Use only the atom and its evidence as ground truth, except where a check says to use general domain knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the key, answer "hold" for KEY_CORRECT and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure, fail and explain.
- For G1_SINGLE_ATOM and KEY_CORRECT, answer as a test taker who knows ONLY the atom: if that person could not reach the key (including a False/No key) with certainty, fail.
- "why" is required for every value other than pass; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets):
- G1_SINGLE_ATOM [pass / fail]: The correct answer follows from this atom alone, without other background knowledge. fail if answering also needs a fact the atom does not state (e.g. the atom says A affects B, but the question needs to know in which direction or in which situation).
- G2_NO_COMPUTATION [pass / fail]: No calculation, proof, or combination of several facts is needed (no L2 application).
- G3_FINAL_ANSWER [pass / fail]: The answer can be graded as a label, an option, or the presence of key points.
- KEY_CORRECT [pass / fail]: The answer key agrees with the atom and evidence. For a False/No target, the atom must rule the statement out: the item must contradict the atom, not merely say something the atom does not mention. fail if the statement could still be true while the atom is true (e.g. the atom states one hypothesis and the item states a rival hypothesis the atom does not exclude).
- SINGLE_ANSWER [pass / fail]: Exactly one option or label is correct. For this check only, also use general domain knowledge: fail if another option or label could be correct in reality.
- NO_LEAK [pass / fail]: The item does not give away its answer. OPEN/MCQ/YN: the question does not state or closely paraphrase the answer. TF: the statement itself is what is tested, so a paraphrase of the atom is fine; fail only for hints outside the claim (e.g. 'as is well known').
- KP_IN_ATOM [pass / fail]: Every key point is part of the atom.
- YN_CASE_FORMAT [pass / fail]: The case describes a concrete object (patient, system, dataset, mathematical object) and the question asks whether THE CASE is an instance of / exhibits the property. fail = it asks whether a claim, view, belief, or approach is correct, consistent, or possible.
- ONE_ELEMENT_CHANGE [pass / fail]: An element is one slot of the claim: a quantity, a direction, a condition, an entity or role, or a negation. Count slots, not words: rewording several words to change one idea is one element; changing two independent slots (e.g. what is reported AND how the process ends) is two. TF False: the statement differs from the atom in exactly one element. MCQ: each distractor differs from the correct option in exactly one element, and the three distractors change different elements. Name the changed element(s) in why when failing.
- NO_SOURCE_REF [pass / fail]: The item does not point to a source: no book, authors, chapter, year, 'the review', 'this study', 'according to the text'. Named laws, scales, or standards are allowed.
- AUTHOR_OPINION_RESOLVED [pass / fail]: If the atom is the authors' opinion or one study's finding, the item must not ask it as a universal fact, and its answer must still be fixed without the book. pass if the atom is a general claim.
- NO_INTRA_CARD_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other item in this batch tests the same knowledge (one answer implies the other). If two overlap, fail only the one listed later and put the other item's id in cite.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<item_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}}

CONCEPT: Knowledge Graph Management System

ITEMS:
- KGBDP-C10-S1-02-M2-TF | FORMAT: TF | ANSWER KEY: True
  CHECKS: G1_SINGLE_ATOM, G2_NO_COMPUTATION, G3_FINAL_ANSWER, KEY_CORRECT, SINGLE_ANSWER, NO_LEAK, NO_SOURCE_REF, AUTHOR_OPINION_RESOLVED, NO_INTRA_CARD_OVERLAP
  ATOM: Bellomarini et al. define a knowledge graph as a semi-structured datamodel with three components: a ground extensional component (relational constructs for schema and data, modelable as graphs or generalizations), an intensional component (inference rules over the ground extensional constructs), and a derived extensional component produced by applying the rules to the ground component through reasoning.
  EVIDENCE: “A semi-structured datamodel characterized by three components: (i) a ground extensional component, that is, a set of relational constructs for schema and data (which can be effectively modeled as graphs or generalizations thereof); (ii) an intensional component, that is, a set of inference rules over the constructs of the ground extensional component; (iii) a derived extensional component that can be produced as the result of the application of the inference rules over the ground extensional component (with the so-called “reasoning” process).” – Bellomarini et al., 2019 – [40].
  ITEM:
    True or False?
    "One definition describes a knowledge graph as a semi-structured data model with three components. The first is a ground extensional component of relational constructs for schema and data, which can be modeled as graphs or generalizations of graphs. The second is an intensional component of inference rules over those ground constructs. The third is a derived extensional component obtained by applying the rules to the ground component through reasoning."
- KGBDP-C10-S2-03-M3-YN | FORMAT: YN | ANSWER KEY: No
  CHECKS: G1_SINGLE_ATOM, G2_NO_COMPUTATION, G3_FINAL_ANSWER, KEY_CORRECT, SINGLE_ANSWER, NO_LEAK, YN_CASE_FORMAT, NO_SOURCE_REF, AUTHOR_OPINION_RESOLVED, NO_INTRA_CARD_OVERLAP
  ATOM: The Vadalog system was presented in technical detail with a focus on algorithms and data structures that meet the requirements of high expressive power, ontological reasoning and low complexity at the same time.
  EVIDENCE: They subsequently presented the Vadalog system [38] in more technical detail, focusing on algorithms and data structures to meet the requirement on high expressive power, ontological reasoning and low complexity at the same time.
  ITEM:
    A research group builds a reasoning engine for knowledge graphs. Its language supports full recursion (at least Datalog) and OWL 2 QL-style ontological reasoning. However, even its core fragment has reasoning that is EXPTIME-hard in data complexity. The group presents its algorithms and data structures in technical detail.
    Does this engine meet the combination of high expressive power, ontological reasoning and low complexity that the Vadalog system's algorithms and data structures were designed to meet at the same time? (Yes/No)
- KGBDP-C10-S3-02-M2-TF | FORMAT: TF | ANSWER KEY: True
  CHECKS: G1_SINGLE_ATOM, G2_NO_COMPUTATION, G3_FINAL_ANSWER, KEY_CORRECT, SINGLE_ANSWER, NO_LEAK, NO_SOURCE_REF, AUTHOR_OPINION_RESOLVED, NO_INTRA_CARD_OVERLAP
  ATOM: The authors treat question answering, recommender systems, entity resolution and link prediction as application services because they offer a well-defined application, in contrast to a management system that offers a query language supporting such applications.
  EVIDENCE: Here, we will consider all of four of these as application services as they clearly offer a well-defined application compared to a management system offering a query language that supports such applications.
  ITEM:
    True or False?
    "Question answering, recommender systems, entity resolution and link prediction can all be classified as application services, because each offers a clearly defined application. A management system, by contrast, offers a query language that supports such applications."
